record.paper_title: Basic kinetic wealth-exchange models: common features and open problems
record.context_brief: Analytical formula for generalized C-model Gamma parameter
record.original_question: In the generalized homogeneous C-model where the stochastic fraction of wealth lost by an agent in a trade is constrained between lower and upper bounds, equivalently by saving parameters λ and λ′ satisfying λ < λ′ < 1, and simulations find equilibrium wealth distributions that are well fitted by the same Gamma distribution, can one derive a simple analytical formula for the Gamma-distribution shape parameter n as a function of λ and λ′?

evidence.quote: One can also define a parameter λ′ = 1−ω′, with λ < λ′ < 1, representing the maximum fraction of saved wealth

We have performed numerical simulations for a set of combinations of parameters (λ, λ′) and found that the equilibrium distributions are always well fitted by the same Γ-distribution (5). However, we have not found a simple analytical formula for fitting the dependence of the parameter n on the saving parameters λ and λ′.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a kinetic wealth-exchange model defined as follows. There are N agents, each holding a non-negative wealth x_i, with total wealth conserved. At each elementary step, two agents i and j are chosen at random and trade according to
  x_i' = x_i - Δx,    x_j' = x_j + Δx,
where the transferred amount Δx is a stochastic fraction of one agent's wealth. In the generalized homogeneous "C-model" version, the fraction ω of wealth that agent i risks losing in a trade is drawn uniformly at random from an interval [ω', ω] with 0 < ω' < ω < 1, equivalently parametrized by two saving propensities
  λ = 1 − ω,    λ' = 1 − ω',   with   λ < λ' < 1,
so that λ is the minimum saved fraction and λ' is the maximum saved fraction. The transferred amount is Δx = ε · ω̃ · x_i, where ω̃ is drawn uniformly from [ω', ω] and ε ∈ {0,1} (or an analogous fair-trade rule) ensures conservation of wealth and an unbiased exchange.

Numerical simulations indicate that, for every admissible pair (λ, λ'), the stationary one-agent wealth distribution P(x) is well fitted by a Gamma distribution
  f_n(x) = (n^n / Γ(n)) · x^{n−1} · e^{−n x}   (with mean wealth normalized to 1),
for some shape parameter n = n(λ, λ').

Problem: Derive a closed-form analytical expression for the Gamma-distribution shape parameter n as a function of the two saving parameters λ and λ' (reducing, when λ = λ', to the known formula n(λ) = 1 + 3λ/(1−λ) for the standard homogeneous saving model).
artifact.status_search_result: A web search did not surface any work providing an explicit closed-form expression for the Gamma shape parameter n(λ, λ') of the generalized homogeneous C-model with bounded saving propensities. Related literature on generalized money/wealth-exchange models (e.g., hypergraph generalizations and saving-propensity models) studies Gamma limit distributions but does not appear to give the requested analytical formula in terms of (λ, λ'). The status is therefore not clearly established from public sources.

status_evidence.title: Limiting distributions of generalized money exchange models on hypergraphs
status_evidence.snippet: Generalized versions of immediate exchange and uniform saving models; asymptotic wealth distribution converges to a Gamma or exponential distribution depending on weight function.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work on generalized money-exchange models studies Gamma limit distributions but does not provide an explicit n(λ, λ') formula for the C-model with bounded saving propensities.

status_evidence.title: Wealth distribution: To be or not to be a Gamma?
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses whether equilibrium wealth distributions in kinetic exchange models are Gamma-distributed.
status_evidence.claim: The question of exact Gamma fits in saving-propensity kinetic models remains an active topic; no closed form for the bounded two-parameter version is reported.
